headline_marked: 10 killed as [[Israeli strikes hit Lebanon]] hours after ceasefire
headline: 10 killed as Israeli strikes hit Lebanon hours after ceasefire
summary: The attacks target multiple locations in the south and Bekaa Valley, highlighting the fragility of a truce intended to halt escalating violence.
details: Israeli warplanes and drones struck multiple locations in southern Lebanon and the Bekaa Valley on Saturday, killing at least 10 people.
The strikes occurred just hours after a ceasefire with Hezbollah took effect, which had been agreed upon on Friday.
Israel stated the attacks were a response to over 50 projectiles fired by Hezbollah at Israeli forces in southern Lebanon overnight.
One of the deadliest strikes hit a three-storey residential building in the town of Barish, killing a father, mother, and their two children.
The Lebanese army reported that an Israeli strike killed a soldier on the Kfarrumman-Nabatieh road, accusing Israel of undermining stability.
Hezbollah officials stated they would not allow Israel freedom of movement in Lebanese territory, maintaining that resistance remains legitimate.
Lebanon's health ministry reports that 3,912 people have been killed in Israeli attacks since March 2, including medics, women, and children.
The violence underscores the fragility of an interim peace deal between the US and Iran, which hinges on an end to the conflict in Lebanon.
caption:
10 people killed in Lebanon just hours after a ceasefire took effect.

Israeli warplanes and drones struck multiple locations in southern Lebanon and the Bekaa Valley on Saturday, killing at least 10 people.

The strikes occurred just hours after a ceasefire with Hezbollah took effect, which had been agreed upon on Friday.

Israel stated the attacks were a response to over 50 projectiles fired by Hezbollah at Israeli forces in southern Lebanon overnight.

One of the deadliest strikes hit a three-storey residential building in the town of Barish, killing a father, mother, and their two children.

The Lebanese army reported that an Israeli strike killed a soldier on the Kfarrumman-Nabatieh road, accusing Israel of undermining stability.

Hezbollah officials stated they would not allow Israel freedom of movement in Lebanese territory, maintaining that resistance remains legitimate.

Lebanon's health ministry reports that 3,912 people have been killed in Israeli attacks since March 2, including medics, women, and children.

The violence underscores the fragility of an interim peace deal between the US and Iran, which hinges on an end to the conflict in Lebanon.

Source: bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV
